judged_text: When no destinationCalendar entry matches the passed credentialId, selectedCalendar is undefined and the event silently falls back to calendarId 'primary' instead of the user-selected calendar. Users with multiple Google credentials/destination calendars get the booking created on their primary calendar (visible on their main schedule, potentially shared) whenever the credentialId match fails, with no error or warning — a silent privacy leak of booking details into an unintended calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts#createEvent`, the PR changes calendar selection to `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and then calls `calendar.events.insert` with `calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`. If no destinationCalendar entry matches the passed `credentialId`, `selectedCalendar` becomes `undefined` and the event is created on the Google account’s primary calendar with no error/warning. Previously (when destinationCalendar was a single object) providing `destinationCalendar.externalId` would always be used; this diff introduces the silent fallback behavior when the credentialId mapping fails, matching the finding’s described risk.
